symptom: Synthetic source-path analysis identified that v0.1 Forward Vault validated and compared claimed instants using mutable ambient Date.parse and RegExp.exec. A later mutation of Date.parse could make a reversed enrollment interval appear equal and pass admission; a mutation of RegExp.exec could deny otherwise valid timestamps. This is research-only syntactic integrity, not an observed attack or evidence of authenticated time.
lesson: Version-specific claimed-time validation can diverge under ambient JavaScript intrinsic mutation even when a newer bounded parser is protected. Reuse the pinned shared parser and comparator rather than maintaining a second mutable chronology path. Claimed timestamps remain unauthenticated.
guardrail: Use the existing bounded and module-initialization-pinned v0.2 claimed-instant helper for v0.1 runtime syntax and submillisecond ordering. Regress reversed enrollment intervals with ambient Date.parse altered and valid enrollment instants with ambient RegExp.exec altered; retain v0.1 schema and all research/production isolation. Never infer K issuer rights, independent finality or scoring authority from green tests.
